name: Tututepec Mixtec
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only subgrouping refs (Josserand 1983; Auderset et al. 2023); no dedicated description found

sources.citation: SIL Mexico, 'Familia mixteca' resource page (mexico.sil.org/es/lengua_cultura/mixteca), accessed 2026-09-17
sources.note: No materials for mtu; no Tututepec variety listed.

sources.citation: Sullivant, J. Ryan. Curriculum vitae (Google Doc linked from jryansullivant.wordpress.com/about, accessed 2026-09-17)
sources.note: Bibliographic record only: lists the 2015 ms. (with PDF link), the 2020 SSILA talk (slides link), the postponed COLOV 9 (2020) talk 'Los cuestionarios lingüísticos del mixteco por Kathryn Josserand', and the AILLA/NEH crowdsourced transcription collection of Josserand's Mixtec surveys (ailla:271571). Archival-research languages include 'Coastal Mixtec [mxt, mtu, mjc, mih]'.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page tutu1243 (Tututepec Mixtec), accessed 2026-09-17
sources.note: Only classification comments (Auderset et al. 2023:13-14; Josserand 1983) and endangerment (Campbell et al. 2022); no descriptive reference. Alternative names: Mixteco de San Pedro Tututepec, Southern Misteko/Mixteco.
No phonology; only Ethnologue intelligibility figures (61% with Ixtayutla, 50% with Pinotepa) and speaker counts (1,020 in 2000).

sources.citation: Auderset, Sandra, Simon J. Greenhill, Christian T. DiCanio & Eric W. Campbell. 2023. Supplementary Material 2 (coding details) to 'Subgrouping in a dialect continuum: A Bayesian phylogenetic analysis of the Mixtecan language family', Journal of Language Evolution 8(1):33-63. Zenodo record 7940497 [Glottolog ref 671112]
sources.note: No stress information. Doculect table (p. 6): tutu11 Villa de Tututepec de Melchor Ocampo, tutu12 San Pedro Tututepec, both tutu1243/mtu. Table 4 (p. 16): San Pedro Tututepec = Josserand's code 'tut', tone marked on <5% of entries, grave-accent notation. No per-variety section for Tututepec (only Josserand 1983 as source). Lexibank CLDF (mixtecansubgrouping v0.4, Zenodo 14001610) confirms every Tututepec form is sourced 'josserand1983mixtec'.

sources.citation: Sullivant, J. Ryan. 2020. A Sketch of Tututepec Mixtec based on 20th Century Historical Sources. Slides presented at the SSILA Annual Meeting, New Orleans, 2 Jan 2020. 20 slides.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Slide 'Profile of Tututepec Mixtec': 'Fairly typical Mixtec phonemic inventories and phonotactic structures' with consonant/vowel chart (V, Vn, VV, VVn) and word templates CVCV, CVV, CV'CV, CV'V; verb-morphology slide: 'tone changes and no change across aspects are possible, but not investigated here'. Sources: Belmar 1902 wordlist; Josserand 1977 surveys (Mesa Mata & Josserand 1977a,b; Nicolás Espinosa & Josserand 1977a,b) at AILLA.

sources.citation: Sullivant, J. Ryan. 2015. Los datos del mixteco de Tututepec en Belmar (1902). Ms., University of Texas at Austin, 13 pp. [Glottolog ref 478224, hhtype wordlist]
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. §1 (p. 2) gives the segmental inventory /p t tʲ tʃ k kʷ ʔ ⁿd β s ʃ m n ɲ l r j; a e i o u ɨ/ 'basado en un análisis del muy parecido mixteco de Jamiltepec (Josserand 1983:188)'; §2.1 'El tono' (p. 2): 'no hay indicación del tono en Belmar (1902), aunque es seguro que MT es una lengua tonal... Este papel no indicará el tono en MT.' Belmar's acute accents (<cáanu>, <chaá>, <yacuí>) are left uninterpreted. 229 items re-analysed with comparison to Chayuco, Jamiltepec and San Juan Colorado forms.

sources.citation: Belmar, Francisco. 1902. Indian tribes of the state of Oaxaca and their languages. Reprinted from Transactions of the International Congress of Americanists 1902, pp. 193-202.
sources.note: Classification essay; Tututepec named only as a prosperous Mixtec city; no phonology. Not the Chatino monograph (Investigaciones sobre la lengua chatina) whose pp. 12-19 hold the Tututepec Mixtec wordlist [Glottolog ref 474682]; that monograph was not found on archive.org or via HathiTrust (Cloudflare-blocked), and its data are reproduced in Sullivant 2015.

sources.citation: Johnson, Audrey F. 1988. A syntactic sketch of Jamiltepec Mixtec. In C. Henry Bradley & Barbara E. Hollenbach (eds.), Studies in the syntax of Mixtecan languages 1 (SIL Publications in Linguistics 83), 11-150. Dallas: SIL/UTA.

sources.note: Johnson (p. 17) proposes that the Santa Cruz and San Pedro Tututepec dialects be considered varieties of Jamiltepec Mixtec; its phonology preliminaries are the nearest published description and would supply a related-variety stress statement (different glottocode jami1235).
